passages.text: “Surely there is a mine for silver and a place where gold is refined.
passages.sermon:
Silver comes from a mine.
People find silver in the earth.
Gold has a place where people refine it.
People purify gold in a special place.
passages.original: כִּ֤י יֵ֣שׁ לַכֶּ֣סֶף מוֹצָ֑א וּ֝מָק֗וֹם לַזָּהָ֥ב יָזֹֽקּוּ׃

passages.text: Iron is taken from the earth, and copper is smelted from ore.
passages.sermon:
Iron comes from the earth.
People take iron out of the ground.
Copper comes from stone.
People melt stone to get copper.
passages.original: בַּ֭רְזֶל מֵעָפָ֣ר יֻקָּ֑ח וְ֝אֶ֗בֶן יָצ֥וּק נְחוּשָֽׁה׃

passages.text: Man puts an end to the darkness; he probes the farthest recesses for ore in deepest darkness.
passages.sermon:
Man explores the earth.
Man searches for valuable things.
Man puts an end to darkness.
Man investigates every limit.
Man looks for ore in the deepest places.
Man searches in places of thick darkness and shadow of death.
passages.original: קֵ֤ץ׀ שָׂ֤ם לַחֹ֗שֶׁךְ וּֽלְכָל־ תַּ֭כְלִית ה֣וּא חוֹקֵ֑ר אֶ֖בֶן אֹ֣פֶל וְצַלְמָֽוֶת׃

passages.text: Far from human habitation he cuts a shaft in places forgotten by the foot of man. Far from men he dangles and sways.
passages.sermon:
A man works far from where people live.
He cuts a shaft in a lonely place.
No one walks there.
People have forgotten these places.
He moves far from other men.
He dangles and sways alone.
passages.original: פָּ֤רַץ נַ֨חַל׀ מֵֽעִם־ גָּ֗ר הַֽנִּשְׁכָּחִ֥ים מִנִּי־ רָ֑גֶל דַּ֖לּוּ מֵאֱנ֣וֹשׁ נָֽעוּ׃

passages.text: Food may come from the earth, but from below it is transformed as by fire.
passages.sermon:
The earth gives food.
People take bread from the ground.
Below the earth, things change.
Under the surface, the earth is transformed.
Fire changes what is below the ground.
passages.original: אֶ֗רֶץ מִמֶּ֥נָּה יֵֽצֵא־ לָ֑חֶם וְ֝תַחְתֶּ֗יהָ נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ כְּמוֹ־ אֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: Its rocks are the source of sapphires, containing flecks of gold.
passages.sermon: This place has rocks.\r\nThese rocks contain sapphires.\r\nThese rocks also have flecks of gold.
passages.original: מְקוֹם־ סַפִּ֥יר אֲבָנֶ֑יהָ וְעַפְרֹ֖ת זָהָ֣ב לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: No bird of prey knows that path; no falcon’s eye has seen it.
passages.sermon: A path exists deep in the earth.\r\nNo bird of prey knows this path.\r\nNo falcon has ever seen it.
passages.original: נָ֭תִיב לֹֽא־ יְדָ֣עוֹ עָ֑יִט וְלֹ֥א שְׁ֝זָפַ֗תּוּ עֵ֣ין אַיָּֽה׃

passages.text: Proud beasts have never trodden it; no lion has ever prowled over it.
passages.sermon: No proud beast has ever walked on this path.\r\nNo lion has ever crossed over it.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ הִדְרִיכֻ֥הוּ בְנֵי־ שָׁ֑חַץ לֹֽא־ עָדָ֖ה עָלָ֣יו שָֽׁחַל׃

passages.text: The miner strikes the flint; he overturns mountains at their base.
passages.sermon:
A miner works with stone.
He strikes the hard flint with his hand.
He overturns mountains.
He does this at the very base of the mountains.
passages.original: בַּֽ֭חַלָּמִישׁ שָׁלַ֣ח יָד֑וֹ הָפַ֖ךְ מִשֹּׁ֣רֶשׁ הָרִֽים׃

passages.text: He hews out channels in the rocks, and his eyes spot every treasure.
passages.sermon:
A miner works in the rocks.
He cuts channels through the stone.
He looks carefully at what he finds.
He sees every valuable thing.
passages.original: בַּ֭צּוּרוֹת יְאֹרִ֣ים בִּקֵּ֑עַ וְכָל־ יְ֝קָ֗ר רָאֲתָ֥ה עֵינֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He stops up the sources of the streams to bring what is hidden to light.
passages.sermon:
A miner works deep in the earth.
He blocks the sources of the streams.
He does this to uncover what is hidden.
He brings hidden things into the light.
passages.original: מִ֭בְּכִי נְהָר֣וֹת חִבֵּ֑שׁ וְ֝תַעֲלֻמָ֗הּ יֹ֣צִא אֽוֹר׃פ

passages.text: But where can wisdom be found, and where does understanding dwell?
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is very important.
Wisdom is hard to find.
No one knows where to find wisdom.
No one knows where understanding lives.
People search for wisdom.
People do not know its place.
passages.original: וְֽ֭הַחָכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תִּמָּצֵ֑א וְאֵ֥י זֶ֝ה מְק֣וֹם בִּינָֽה׃

passages.text: No man can know its value, nor is it found in the land of the living.
passages.sermon: No person can understand the value of wisdom.\r\nNo one can find wisdom among the living on earth.
passages.original: לֹא־ יָדַ֣ע אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עֶרְכָּ֑הּ וְלֹ֥א תִ֝מָּצֵ֗א בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הַֽחַיִּֽים׃

passages.text: The ocean depths say, ‘It is not in me,’ while the sea declares, ‘It is not with me.’
passages.sermon:
The ocean depths speak.
They say, “Wisdom is not in me.”
The sea also speaks.
It says, “Wisdom is not with me.”
passages.original: תְּה֣וֹם אָ֭מַר לֹ֣א בִי־ הִ֑יא וְיָ֥ם אָ֝מַ֗ר אֵ֣ין עִמָּדִֽי׃

passages.text: It cannot be bought with gold, nor can its price be weighed out in silver.
passages.sermon: No one can buy wisdom with gold.\r\nNo one can measure its price with silver.
passages.original: לֹא־ יֻתַּ֣ן סְג֣וֹר תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ וְלֹ֥א יִ֝שָּׁקֵ֗ל כֶּ֣סֶף מְחִירָֽהּ׃

passages.text: It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.
passages.sermon:
This passage speaks about wisdom.
Wisdom is extremely valuable.
No one can measure wisdom by gold from Ophir.
No one can compare wisdom to precious onyx.
No one can compare wisdom to sapphire.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תְ֭סֻלֶּה בְּכֶ֣תֶם אוֹפִ֑יר בְּשֹׁ֖הַם יָקָ֣ר וְסַפִּֽיר׃

passages.text: Neither gold nor crystal can compare to it, nor jewels of fine gold be exchanged for it.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is extremely valuable.
Gold cannot compare to wisdom.
Crystal cannot compare to wisdom.
You cannot exchange wisdom for jewels of fine gold.
passages.original: לֹא־ יַעַרְכֶ֣נָּה זָ֭הָב וּזְכוֹכִ֑ית וּתְמ֖וּרָתָ֣הּ כְּלִי־ פָֽז׃

passages.text: Coral and quartz are unworthy of mention; the price of wisdom is beyond rubies.
passages.sermon:
Coral is not important when compared to wisdom.
Quartz is not important when compared to wisdom.
Wisdom is more valuable than rubies.
No one can measure the worth of wisdom with precious stones.
passages.original: רָאמ֣וֹת וְ֭גָבִישׁ לֹ֣א יִזָּכֵ֑ר וּמֶ֥שֶׁךְ חָ֝כְמָ֗ה מִפְּנִינִֽים׃

passages.text: Topaz from Cush cannot compare to it, nor can it be valued in pure gold.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is more valuable than any treasure.
\r\nTopaz from Cush cannot compare to wisdom.
\r\nPure gold cannot equal wisdom.
\r\nNo one can measure wisdom by gold.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ יַ֭עַרְכֶנָּה פִּטְדַת־ כּ֑וּשׁ בְּכֶ֥תֶם טָ֝ה֗וֹר לֹ֣א תְסֻלֶּֽה׃פ

passages.text: From where then does wisdom come, and where does understanding dwell?
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is very valuable.
Wisdom is more valuable than coral, quartz, or rubies.
Wisdom is more valuable than topaz or pure gold.
No one can easily find wisdom.
No one knows where wisdom comes from.
No one knows where understanding lives.
passages.original: וְֽ֭הַחָכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תָּב֑וֹא וְאֵ֥י זֶ֝֗ה מְק֣וֹם בִּינָֽה׃

passages.text: It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing and concealed from the birds of the air.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is hidden from every living thing.
No creature can see it.
Wisdom is also concealed from the birds in the sky.
Even those who fly above cannot find it.
passages.original: וְֽ֭נֶעֶלְמָה מֵעֵינֵ֣י כָל־ חָ֑י וּמֵע֖וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם נִסְתָּֽרָה׃

passages.text: Abaddon and Death say, ‘We have heard a rumor about it.’
passages.sermon:
Abaddon is the place of destruction.
Death is the end of life.
Abaddon and Death speak.
They say, “We have heard a rumor about wisdom.”
They do not know wisdom directly.
They only hear about wisdom from others.
passages.original: אֲבַדּ֣וֹן וָ֭מָוֶת אָ֣מְר֑וּ בְּ֝אָזְנֵ֗ינוּ שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ שִׁמְעָֽהּ׃

passages.text: But God understands its way, and He knows its place.
passages.sermon: God understands the way of wisdom.\r\nGod knows the place of wisdom.
passages.original: אֱ֭לֹהִים הֵבִ֣ין דַּרְכָּ֑הּ וְ֝ה֗וּא יָדַ֥ע אֶת־ מְקוֹמָֽהּ׃

passages.text: For He looks to the ends of the earth and sees everything under the heavens.
passages.sermon:
God sees everything.
God looks to the ends of the earth.
God sees all things under the heavens.
passages.original: כִּי־ ה֭וּא לִקְצוֹת־ הָאָ֣רֶץ יַבִּ֑יט תַּ֖חַת כָּל־ הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם יִרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: When God fixed the weight of the wind and measured out the waters, when He set a limit for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt, then He looked at wisdom and appraised it; He established it and searched it out.
passages.sermon:
God fixed the weight of the wind.
God measured the waters.
God set a limit for the rain.
God made a path for the thunderbolt.
Then God looked at wisdom.
God appraised wisdom.
God established wisdom.
God searched out wisdom.
passages.original: לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָר֣וּחַ מִשְׁקָ֑ל וּ֝מַ֗יִם תִּכֵּ֥ן בְּמִדָּֽה׃ בַּעֲשֹׂת֣וֹ לַמָּטָ֣ר חֹ֑ק וְ֝דֶ֗רֶךְ לַחֲזִ֥יז קֹלֽוֹת׃ אָ֣ז רָ֭אָהּ וַֽיְסַפְּרָ֑הּ הֱ֝כִינָ֗הּ וְגַם־ חֲקָרָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And He said to man, ‘Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.’ ”
passages.sermon: God spoke to man.\r\nGod said, “The fear of the Lord is wisdom.\r\nTo turn away from evil is understanding.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר׀ לָֽאָדָ֗ם הֵ֤ן יִרְאַ֣ת אֲ֭דֹנָי הִ֣יא חָכְמָ֑ה וְס֖וּר מֵרָ֣ע בִּינָֽה׃ס
